paper.title: From Passive Execution to Active Exploration: Agentic Embodied Manipulation in Realistic Environments
paper.central_claim: An agent-based active-exploration framework (an OpenClaw-based planning module, a perception module with object recognition/localization/OCR, and an execution module of low-level skills) with fine-grained perception-execution interleaving (one atomic operation, then re-perceive) lets a Franka arm complete a real Find-and-Place task with initially invisible targets, distractors and category-guided search, improving robustness and adaptability over passive execution.
paper.claim_scope_note: One real-world task family (two cabinets, pear toy variants, lemon distractors); success rates only, no trial counts, no baselines, no ablations.

evidence.quote: However, most existing embodied manipulation frameworks still follow a largely passive execution paradigm.
While some planning-based methods [ 1 , 3 , 4 , 7 ] have considered such scenarios, they often rely on carefully engineered modules and less generalizable paradigms.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest neighbours are cited only by number and dismissed in one sentence; none is described or compared.

evidence.quote: It extracts task-relevant information through object recognition, target localization, optical character recognition (OCR), and scene-level semantic understanding.
evidence.support_explanation: Perception module contents named without models or interface.

evidence.quote: Instead of executing a complete action sequence based on the initial observation, the robot invokes the execution module for one atomic operation and calls the perception module to update its understanding of the environment.
evidence.support_explanation: Core operation: one atomic operation then re-perceive.

evidence.quote: The overall system is built upon OpenClaw, which serves as the agentic framework and planning module for high-level task reasoning.
evidence.support_explanation: Planner is an agentic framework; the underlying LLM/VLM is not named.

evidence.quote: The perception and execution modules are implemented locally.
evidence.support_explanation: No further specification of perception models or execution skills (scripted, learned, VLA).

evidence.quote: We deploy the proposed framework on a Franka robotic arm in the real world.
we evaluate one representative setting where the pear toy is specified as the target object

A trial is considered successful only if the robot correctly identifies the relevant cabinet, searches the drawers until the target object is found, grasps the target object, and places it into the box.
evidence.support_explanation: Success criterion is defined; who judged it and how many trials are not stated.

evidence.quote: Failure cases include selecting the wrong cabinet, stopping before finding the target, grasping a distractor, or failing to complete the final placement.
evidence.support_explanation: Failure categories listed but never counted.

evidence.quote: Target Object Variant 1 96.0 94.0 Target Object Variant 2 96.0 95.0 Target Object Variant 3 95.0 94.0 Overall 95.7 94.3
evidence.support_explanation: Only results: success rates per variant, without/with distractors; no counts, no baseline.

evidence.quote: demonstrating that the proposed active exploration strategy can robustly identify, search for, and manipulate the intended target in cluttered and ambiguous environments
evidence.support_explanation: Interpretation stronger than a table of five numbers for one framework without controls.

evidence.quote: Experimental results demonstrate that our framework improves the robustness and adaptability of embodied manipulation in challenging scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: Comparative claim ('improves') with no comparison in the paper.

evidence.quote: The entire system can run on a consumer-grade NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU
evidence.support_explanation: Only cost-related statement; no latency, calls, tokens or time per trial.

The overall values equal the means of the three variant values, and 95.0 requires n to be a multiple of 20 while 96.0 requires a multiple of 25, so equal n=100 per cell is consistent; but no n is stated (our inference).

evidence.quote: The target object is placed inside an unknown drawer and is not visible from the initial observation.
evidence.support_explanation: Task setting: hidden target in an unknown drawer.

evidence.quote: Each cabinet is associated with a different object category and marked with a category label on its top surface.
evidence.support_explanation: Category labels on cabinets reduce the search to one cabinet; OCR is the cue.

signatures.object: Control flow of a manipulation agent: passive full-plan execution replaced by a plan/perceive/execute loop with one atomic operation per cycle
signatures.information: User instruction, current visual observation and interaction history to the planner; perception returns object recognition, localisation, OCR and scene-level understanding; planner backbone, prompts and history format are unspecified; ground-truth state not stated
signatures.operation: Planner picks the next exploratory or manipulative operation (inspect label, open drawer, pick, close drawer, place); execution module performs it; perception re-analyses and returns visibility, scene change and task progress; planner decides whether the subgoal is done, to explore further or to proceed
signatures.output: Sequence of atomic operations until the target is placed in the box
signatures.conditions: Real Franka tabletop, two multi-drawer cabinets with category labels, known skill set (open/close drawer, pick, place)
signatures.feedback: Perception-derived visibility and progress after every atomic operation
signatures.selection_rule_data: Planner judgement; no stated acceptance, retry or hand-back rule
signatures.persistence: Interaction history in the planner context (format unspecified)
signatures.later_use: Subsequent planning decisions in the same episode
signatures.claimed_effect: 94.3-96.0% success across three target variants with and without distractors
signatures.failure_boundary: Failure categories named but uncounted; limitations section absent

retention_trace.explanation: A static agent framework evaluated on one task; no learning, memory across episodes or harness revision is claimed.

gap.author_gap: Embodied manipulation frameworks assume visible, uncluttered targets and execute predefined plans (passive execution); real scenes have occlusion, distractors, textual cues and initially invisible targets, and planning-based remedies rely on carefully engineered modules.
gap.checked_gap: The limitation is real and well motivated in prose, but the nearest planning-based neighbours are only numbered, not described or compared, and there is no related-work section; the shortfall of existing agentic systems on this specific task is asserted, not shown.
gap.lineage: Agentic planner + VLA/skill executors -> planning-based exploration systems [1,3,4,7] (unnamed) -> this framework (planner, perception, execution with atomic-step interleaving)

closest_adjacent.remaining: described only as relying on carefully engineered modules and less generalizable paradigms

gap.residue: A modular agent that re-perceives after each atomic operation for hidden-target Find-and-Place
gap.stakes: Stated only qualitatively (gap between laboratory and real-world deployment)
gap.remaining_gap: Everything about baselines, ablations, other tasks and embodiments, and planner-backbone dependence
unresolved: Which prior system, if any, fails on this task and how

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Step 1 responsibility boundary: planner reasons, perception module extracts scene information, execution module performs skills (stated but not specified). Step 2 typed machine-checkable artifact at each handoff: not specified (no formats for subtask, perception output or feedback). Step 3 close the loop with an obtainable signal during construction: perception feedback after every atomic operation (present). Step 4 ablate the verification or feedback step to a baseline: absent. Step 5 cost and validation beyond toy instances: only an RTX 3090 statement; one task (partial/absent).
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: boundary (partial), obtainable signals (met), single load-bearing mechanism ablated to a named baseline (not met), reusable capital (not applicable). Failure: assembly of off-the-shelf parts (present: OpenClaw plus local modules), hand-tailored to one benchmark (present: one scenario), no ablation isolating the decomposition (present), cost unmeasured (present).
matches.reason: The closest of the 15 mains for a planner delegating to perception and execution modules with per-step re-observation; the match is weak because typed artifacts, solver feedback and ablation are not shown. Not forced to outside_taxonomy because decomposition into atomic operations with per-operation re-perception is the executed core.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: C25's delegation of sub-problems to specialised modules corresponds to the planner emitting atomic operation units that a separate execution module performs.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K104 assumes a deterministic or frozen executor over a semantic action vocabulary; the paper does not specify the executor or the vocabulary beyond three examples.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Structured scene information from a perception module (recognition, localisation, OCR) handed to the planner corresponds to image-to-text conversion for the planner.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K109 presumes a frozen VLM converter and a text-only planner; the perception module here is unspecified and the planner may see images.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Real-robot closed-loop execution is described, but per-task trial counts are not reported (EVIDENCE.md requires counts and success rates for online credit); results are percentages without denominators, baselines or ablations, which we treat as insufficient for online. Would become online if counts are supplied.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: The authors report about 94-96% success for their planner/perception/execution framework on a single real Franka hidden-object Find-and-Place scenario with three pear-toy variants, with and without lemon distractors; trial counts, controls and ablations are absent, so no improvement or mechanism attribution is supported.
unresolved: Trial counts and who judged success
Development use of the evaluated variants
assessment.reproduction_note: All results are author-reported; nothing was run by us.

G.reason: A real but generic limitation (passive execution) is stated; nearest planning-based methods are only numbered and dismissed in one sentence, no related work is discussed, and the residual problem is not tied to a measured failure.

M.reason: The logic (each atomic operation changes what is visible, so re-perceive before the next decision) is coherent and fits the hidden-target problem, but it is generic, assumptions about perception quality and planner reliability are unexamined, and no distinguishing prediction is tested.

X.reason: Only the module roles and a three-example operation vocabulary are described; planner backbone, prompts, perception models, execution skills, history format, retry/hand-back rules and failure handling are missing, so the operation chain cannot be rebuilt.

measurement.reason: A success criterion is defined and failure categories are listed, but no trial counts, no statement of who judged outcomes, and no per-category failure counts (anchor v2: criterion present but denominators absent -> low band).

causality.reason: The central comparative claim ('improves ... over passive execution') has no baseline, no passive-execution control, no interleaving ablation and no backbone variation in the complete paper; the distractor condition is a robustness check, not a control.
